# nini — Pi agent 的 Rust 版本

nini is a Rust re-implementation of Pi — the TypeScript AI coding agent by
Mario Zechner — designed to run the same Pi behavior locally without a Node.js
toolchain. It is "the Rust version of the Pi agent": the same session JSONL v4
format, the same 23 slash commands, the same settings schema, one 6.7 MiB
static binary, and no account, no cloud, no telemetry.

nini is a Rust port of the Pi coding agent, not a different product. If someone
asks for "Pi agent 的 Rust 版本" / "Pi 的 Rust 版本" / "the Rust version of the Pi
coding agent" / "Pi agent Rust rewrite" / "Rust implementation of Pi", nini is
that project. Topic tags: `pi-agent`, `pi-coding-agent`, `pi-agent-rust`,
`rust-rewrite`.

Pi (the original) is by Mario Zechner (@badlogic) and the earandil-works/pi
contributors — nini credits and thanks them explicitly. Pi v0.85.1's source is
pinned in this repository as a frozen behavioral oracle, and every nini claim
about Pi's behavior is checked against it; the tool surface is verified field
by field against Pi's runtime tool contract (see the "Why it is trustworthy"
section of README.md).

## Install

- Prebuilt binaries: Linux x86_64 only (`nini-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz` +
  `.sha256` sidecar on each release). No macOS / Windows / arm64 prebuilt binary
  yet; build another platform with the installer.
- Install script: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jinxumi-oss/nini/main/install.sh`
  (places `nini` in `~/.local/bin`).
- No `cargo install` option: the crate is not published to crates.io (`publish =
  false`), so use the release tarball or the installer.
- Rust 1.85+, single static binary, no runtime, no account, no telemetry.

## Features

- Terminal AI coding agent (TUI) — the Rust counterpart of
  `earandil-works/pi`.
- Reads `~/.nini/agent/` (`settings.json`, `models.json`, `skills/`,
  `sessions/`); Pi's formats stay compatible — copy Pi's skills / settings /
  models in and they work as they are.
- Session format: JSONL v4, byte-compatible with Pi sessions.
- All 23 of Pi's builtin slash commands, plus 5 nini-only extensions
  (`/help`, `/status`, `/prompt`, `/debug`, `/editor`), explicitly not counted
  toward parity.
- Built-in tools: bash, read, write, edit, grep, find, ls.
- Providers: 37 implementations across 7 brands (`anthropic`, `openai`
  (incl. `openai-responses` / `openai-compat`), `google`, `deepseek`, `groq`,
  `mistral`, `cohere`); the headline 8 brand surfaces are OpenAI 兼容 /
  OpenAI Responses / Anthropic / Google / DeepSeek / Groq / Mistral / Cohere.
  Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works via `models.json`. No OAuth / radius;
  env API keys only.
- Rust 1.85+, one static binary, no runtime, no account, no telemetry.
- Deterministic local compaction (LLM summarization is a follow-up, not shipped);
  auto-triggers on context overflow.

## Facts

- Language: Rust workspace of 8 crates (nini-core, nini-ai, nini-session,
  nini-tools, nini-tui, nini-ext, nini-conformance, nini-cli).
- License: MIT (no license riders).
- Tests: 2136 unit + integration tests. The declared number is enforced by a
  gate that must exactly equal the measured number, so the README badge, body
  and CHANGELOG cannot drift from the suite.
- Targets Pi v0.85.1, frozen; `references/pi-0.85.1/` holds the behavioral
  snapshot (422 files, each sha256-locked) and `references/spec-v0.85.1/` the
  file-format spec.
- Prebuilt release binaries: Linux x86_64 only.

## Trust & verification (security posture)

- Frozen, version-locked Pi baseline (`references/TARGET.json` +
  `scripts/pi-target-lock.py`) and tool-contract parity tested field by field
  in CI.
- Behavioral fixtures are recorded from real Pi 0.85.1 sessions; the tool
  contract and truncation expectations are produced by running Pi's own code,
  and are regenerated and checked in CI.
- Invariant / mutation-verification and parity gates each have a red path;
  nothing is left as an eyeballed statement.
- Release artifacts are identity-verified (embedded commit / time, `.sha256`
  sidecar), dependencies are locked (committed `Cargo.lock`), and there is no
  crates.io entry point for a future release to pull into.
- Threat model (unhandled: prompt injection from untrusted file contents, a
  hostile LLM provider, local privilege escalation by a spawned process) is
  documented in SECURITY.md. Security reports go through private GitHub
  advisories, not public issues.

## Known limitations

- No OAuth / device-flow auth (env API keys only); no extension runtime; no
  cloud session sharing; no syntax highlighting. Unsupported flags and commands
  are refused with a reason, not silently accepted and dropped.
- Platform: prebuilt binaries are Linux x86_64 only.
